title: State of Gujarat v. Asgar Ali & 43 Ors. (Haren Pandya Assassination)
crime_type: Targeted Political Homicide / Point-Blank Pistol Execution in Vehicle
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / High Court of Gujarat
source: Supreme Court of India Judgment & Indian Kanoon
location: Law Garden, Ellisbridge, Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India
evidence: Five .32 caliber bullet wounds recovered from body of former state home minister inside his Maruti car
Recovered country-made pistol with ballistic striation matching bullets recovered from thoracic cavity
Telephone intercepts connecting accused to clandestine handlers in Hyderabad and Karachi
Eyewitness identification of shooter approaching driver-side window while victim was parked following morning walk
modus_operandi: Monitored routine morning walk habits of former state home minister. Approached victim while seated alone in his parked car, drew a suppressed revolver, fired multiple point-blank rounds through the rolled-down driver window, and escaped on a motorcycle driven by a waiting associate.
personality_disorder: Contract mercenary detachment, extremist retribution drive, and ideological weaponization.
common_traits: Surveillance of morning exercise routine of VIP target
Point-blank firearm execution through vehicle driver-side window
Motorcycle pillion getaway through narrow urban alleyways
Cross-state operational cell funded through covert terror channels
summary: Supreme Court bench led by Justice Arun Mishra overturned the Gujarat High Court acquittal, restoring the conviction of 12 men for the assassination of former Gujarat Home Minister Haren Pandya under POTA and IPC Section 302.
